text:
Dan: Heads up — p95 regressed on the A100 after the kernel-selector rollout last night. Short prompts (<=128) jumped from ~45ms -> ~82ms. Anyone else seeing this?
Olga: Yep, saw the same in canary. Interestingly it's highly correlated with cold KV misses — if the KV is warm there's no change.
Sanjay: I profiled a few traces. It looks like the new selector causes extra kernel launches for the cold-KV path (more memcpy + kernel_launch overhead). Quick snippet from nsight: 
```
kernel_selector_v2: extra kernel_launch x1.8, memcpy H2D +12%, cudaSync spikes around 1.6ms
A100 (cold-KV): p95 ~82ms
A100 (warm-KV): p95 ~46ms
T4/H100: negligible change
```
Alice: That suggests two knock-on issues: 1) kernel switching cost, and 2) our current batch formation mixes warm & cold KV requests which drags the whole batch tail.
Ben: Exactly — mixed batches amplify the tail. We should avoid mixing cold-KV requests into large latency-sensitive batches.
Dan: Proposal: introduce a KV-aware queue policy + per-GPU token_budget caps to steer batch formation. Concept config: 
```
queue.policy: "kv-aware"
batching.token_budget_by_gpu:
  a100: 4096
  h100: 8192
  l4: 2048
  t4: 2048
  a10: 3072
prefill_kv_on_session_start: false  # default false, opt-in for small models
separate_cold_batches: true
```
Olga: Note on prefill_kv: prewarming reduces tail but increases memory pressure and startup overhead. We should gate it by model size + tenant tier.
Sanjay: I ran a quick sim with separated cold/warm batches and the kv-aware token caps. Results (canary sim):
- A100: p95 cold-path 52ms (was 82ms), warm-path 44ms
- Throughput +7% overall
- KV_hit_rate metric per-batch rose (less cross-contamination)
These are simulated with realistic seq distributions.
Alice: Nice. Can we implement as a config toggle so we can roll back if kernel team finds a fix? Also add a per-batch kv_hit_rate and batch_kv_mix metric so we can observe.
Ben: I can wire the metrics. Suggest naming: runtime.batch.kv_hit_rate, runtime.batch.kv_mix_ratio, runtime.batching.token_budget.{gpu}.
Dan: I'll open a small change: enforce that if any request in a forming batch is detected cold-KV, it either (a) gets its own small batch up to token_budget_cold, or (b) gets priority to form a small dedicated batch faster. Toggle controlled by queue.policy.
Olga: For rollout, canary to dedicated A100 pods first — they show the regression most.
Sanjay: Also flagging kernel team — this is likely fixing symptoms, not the root cause. But quick mitigation is worthwhile to keep latency SLOs. @kernel-team FYI.
Dan: Plan: PR with kv-aware queue + per-GPU token caps + metrics. Canary deploy tonight to a100 region. If metrics look good, roll to H100.
Alice: Thx. Please include a test that simulates mixed warm/cold request streams; that was missing last time.
Dan: Will do. PR: <https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/12345> :shipit:
ci-bot: deploy started for runtime-canary cluster (canary-a100-01).
Ben: Adding a short runbook note for oncall: how to toggle queue.policy back to "default".
Olga: Also capturing baseline traces for post-mortem once kernel team has a fix.
Dan: Great. If canary p95 stays <55ms for A100 cold path, we promote. Leaving this thread open while canary runs.
